answer: Bond curve: each new mining key must post a bond whose price rises with the number of keys registered from the same funding source in the last 30 days, doubling each time. The operator pays: the first key is cheap, but the tenth costs 512 times as much, so a fleet hits a price summit fast. Bonds anchor capital that stays locked while the key mines. Failure case: an attacker who splits funds across fresh wallets still leaves a tundra of tiny new wallets created at once, a cluster the curve prices as one source.
